prompt: A triangle has sides $3$, $5$, and $7$. Find the angle across from the side of length $7$, in degrees.
hint: Three sides and no angles (SSS) means the Law of Cosines, rearranged to hunt for the angle.

hints.text: Three sides and no angles (SSS) means the Law of Cosines, rearranged to hunt for the angle.
Put $7$ in the $c$ spot: $49 = 9 + 25 - 2 \times 3 \times 5 \times \cos C$, so $49 = 34 - 30\cos C$.

explanation: The angle you want is across from the side $7$, so $7$ plays the role of $c$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Predict before you compute
steps: Test the corner against Pythagoras first: 3² + 5² = 34, but 7² = 49.
The far side came out LONGER than a right angle would allow, so the corner must be wider than 90°.
Only an obtuse answer makes sense, and 120° is obtuse — the computation just confirms your prediction.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read the cosine backwards
steps: You end up needing the angle whose cosine is −1/2.
Cosine is positive for sharp angles and negative for wide ones, so the answer is past 90°.
From the special-angle list, cos 60° = 1/2 and cos 120° = −1/2. The answer is 120°.
